exposure: USAID MOMENTUM Safe Surgery in Family Planning and Obstetrics intervention (active follow-up, tailored education, personalized phone conversations)
cohort: Pregnant women with a previous cesarean delivery, divided into a pre-intervention cohort (n=212) and an intervention cohort (n=189), recruited from public hospitals and health centers in Rwanda.
finding: The active follow-up intervention significantly reduced the odds of emergency cesarean delivery by 81% and increased consultation for a delivery plan within 36-38 weeks of gestation.
mod_finding: The active follow-up intervention significantly reduced the odds of emergency cesarean delivery among pregnant women with previous CD scars.
